verdict.headline: After chip stocks' worst week since April 2025, Meta and Tesla results become the next test
verdict.label: Saturday: S&P 500 closed Fri at 7,659.44 (-1.09%, week -1.9%), seven points under 7,666.45; Nasdaq 26,140.03 (week -4.5%); Dow 52,002.41 (week +0.7%); chips -11.4% on the week; VIX ~20; 10Y ~5.085%; Brent $109.86; BTC ~$81,508 Sat (-0.8% in 24h).
verdict.horizon: Monday October 19 through Wednesday October 21, when Tesla and Meta report
verdict.rationale_short:
What happened: no stock, bond or oil market has traded since Friday, when the chip index fell 3.8% for an eighth straight day and 11.4% for the week, its worst week since April 2025. The S&P 500 closed at 7,659.44, seven points below 7,666.45, the level recent reports named as the sign of selling spreading beyond AI. The Nasdaq lost 4.5% on the week while the Dow gained 0.7%. Rates eased rather than rose: the two-year fell about 3 basis points and FedWatch put an October hold above 80%. Brent settled at $109.86 after touching $110. UKMTO logged 12 attacks on ships in the week to October 16, ten inside the Strait of Hormuz, and says most attacks go unreported. Bitcoin, the only market trading, was near $81,508 Saturday morning, down 0.8% in 24 hours and about $1,200 above its $80,320 low.

What it means: the week's selling was concentrated in AI suppliers and in companies that borrowed to build data centres, not spread across the market, and it happened while near-term hike odds fell. That points to doubts about how AI spending is financed rather than to interest rates. The evidence is not one-sided. Jefferies called the CoreWeave selloff overdone and Bank of America described the AI trade as resilient, while Bank of America's Michael Hartnett expects risk aversion to dominate the coming weeks. The break below 7,666.45 came on monthly options-expiry day, so one close does not yet confirm it.

What would change the picture: a close back above 7,666.45 early next week would make Friday look like an options-driven overshoot. A second close below it with the Dow falling more than 1% would show selling spreading past AI. Meta's capital spending plans on Wednesday are the first direct read from a large AI buyer since the selling began; spending held or raised would argue against the slowdown chip prices imply, and a cut would support it. Oil above $110 would add to the inflation pressure that keeps a December hike in play ahead of the October 27-28 Fed meeting. Conviction is low because no market has reopened and several data sources could not be checked directly this morning.
verdict.lede_short: Chip stocks just had their worst week since April 2025, falling 11.4%, and pulled the S&P 500 just under the level it had held all week, while the Dow rose 0.7%. Near-term rate hike odds fell during the selling, so it reflects doubts about how AI spending is financed, not interest rates. A close back above 7,666 on Monday would make Friday look like an options-expiry overshoot; Meta's spending plans on Wednesday are the next real test.
